modeDescriptions.dropPctMode: Remove a random percentage of trades
modeDescriptions.dropBestTrades: Remove top trades to test robustness
modeDescriptions.noiseInjection: Add random noise to trade P/L values
modeDescriptions.costDegradation: Increase costs to test "Edge" / statistical advantage durability

modeExplanations.shuffle: Reorders your trades at random. If the result depends strongly on when each trade occurred, the equity curve changes a lot — meaning your backtest is sensitive to the sequence. Only perturbs the order, not the trades themselves.
modeExplanations.bootstrap: Samples your trades with replacement (some appear multiple times, others not at all). Generates alternative scenarios for what could have happened with a different sample. This is the primary mode for estimating the range of possible outcomes.
modeExplanations.timeSlice: Crops a window from the history and measures the strategy there. If the "Edge" / statistical advantage only worked in a specific period (a regime), windows outside that period will fail. Detects regime dependency.
modeExplanations.dropPctMode: Removes a random percentage of trades. Simulates what would happen if you missed some signals — the strategy should withstand losing some without losing all the "Edge" / statistical advantage.
modeExplanations.dropBestTrades: Removes the top X% most profitable trades. If after removing the best ones the strategy is no longer profitable, the "Edge" / statistical advantage depends on a few outliers. Dangerous: if those outliers don't repeat, the strategy dies.
modeExplanations.dropCluster: Removes a contiguous block of trades (simulates a losing streak, a connection outage, or a broken market period). Measures whether your strategy survives a concentrated bad streak.
modeExplanations.noiseInjection: Adds random noise to each trade (simulates slippage, imperfect fills, timing). Measures how much your result moves under realistic execution variation.
modeExplanations.costDegradation: Increases costs (slippage + commissions) on each trade by a random percentage. Measures what happens if your broker charges more, or if your fills are worse than assumed in the backtest.

bootstrap.blockSize: Size of the block sampled each time. Small blocks (5-10) preserve little temporal context; large blocks (50+) preserve more correlation between nearby trades.

timeSlice.windowPct: What fraction of the history each window covers. Small windows (10-30%) detect regimes better; large windows (60-90%) are less restrictive.

dropPctMode.dropPctMin: Minimum % of trades to remove per simulation. Each sim picks a random value between Min and Max.
dropPctMode.dropPctMax: Maximum % of trades to remove per simulation. Each sim picks a random value between Min and Max.

dropBestTrades.dropBestPct: What % of the most profitable trades to remove. Low (5-10%) is demanding; high (30%+) is brutal and almost always breaks the strategy.
dropBestTrades.dropBestJitter: Random variation around the target %. Without jitter, every sim removes exactly the same trades and the result is deterministic — not really Monte Carlo.

dropCluster.clusterPctMin: Minimum size of the contiguous block to remove, as % of total trades.
dropCluster.clusterPctMax: Maximum size of the contiguous block to remove, as % of total trades.

noiseInjection.noisePct: Noise magnitude as a fraction of your trades' std. 5% is realistic; 30%+ is high stress.

costDegradation.maxCostPct: Maximum extra cost to apply per trade, as % of the trade value. 3% is realistic for liquid futures; 10%+ is stress.

robustness.mcDisabledRolling: Monte Carlo can't be combined with Walk-Forward Rolling

testExplanations.holdoutValidation: Splits your history into two parts: "train" and "validation" (typically 70/30). Optimizes the strategy on "train" only, then runs the best found parameters on "validation" — data the optimization never saw. If "train" results don't hold on "validation", there's overfitting: you memorized the past instead of finding a real "Edge" / statistical advantage.
testExplanations.rollingWalkForward: Unlike the other robustness tests, this one tests your strategy exactly as you loaded it, with its original parameters. It splits your history into several segments (folds) and moves forward in time, validating each segment on data it never saw. It tells you whether its advantage (its edge) holds up on new data or whether it just memorized the past (overfitting), and whether re-optimizing it periodically pays off more than leaving it with the parameters you set.
testExplanations.monteCarloSection: Applies 8 different types of random perturbations to the backtest's trade sequence (reorder, resample, drop trades, add noise, raise costs, crop periods). For each perturbation it runs N simulations and measures how much the "Edge" / statistical advantage moves. The output is a 0-100 score describing how robust the backtest is under plausible variations.
testExplanations.intrabarSimulation: Re-simulates your trades using candles smaller than the chart's timeframe. If you trade on 1h candles but stops/targets could have been hit intra-hour, this test uses 1m (or 3m/5m) candles to verify when each level was actually touched. Detects SL/TP the backtest 'skipped' by only looking at each large candle's close.
